summary: Fedratinib (Inrebic) is a JAK2 inhibitor for intermediate-2/high-risk primary or secondary myelofibrosis. It carries a boxed warning for serious and fatal encephalopathy including Wernicke encephalopathy: thiamine must be checked and repleted before starting and monitored during therapy, and drug held for suspected encephalopathy. Other risks are anaemia/thrombocytopenia, GI effects, hepatotoxicity, amylase/lipase elevation and embryo-fetal toxicity.
indications: Intermediate-2 or high-risk primary or secondary (post-polycythaemia vera or post-essential thrombocythaemia) myelofibrosis

dosage.d: 400 mg once daily continuously (reduce to 200 mg with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or severe renal impairment)
dosage.n: Check and replete thiamine before starting; hold for suspected encephalopathy, severe anaemia/thrombocytopenia or hepatotoxicity

admin: Take exactly as prescribed; do not crush, split or chew unless labeling allows
Take at the same time(s) each day; if a dose is missed follow the missed-dose rule - do not double
Report interacting new medicines including antifungals, anti-TB drugs, antiepileptics and St John's wort (CYP3A4)
Store in the original container with desiccant where supplied; protect from moisture
moa: Fedratinib is a selective JAK2 inhibitor that blocks JAK2-STAT signalling driving myelofibrosis proliferation, reducing splenomegaly and symptom burden. Off-target thiamine-transporter inhibition is thought to underlie the Wernicke-encephalopathy risk.

monitor: Thiamine levels and Wernicke signs (confusion, ataxia, eye signs)

preg: No adequate human data. Based on mechanism, fetal harm is expected. Verify pregnancy status before starting; advise effective contraception during treatment and for the specified period after the last dose. Use in pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential fetal risk.
lact: No data on presence in human milk. Because of potential serious adverse reactions in the breastfed infant, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for the specified period after the last dose.
renal: Mild-moderate impairment: no routine change unless labeled; severe: limited data - monitor for exaggerated toxicity and dehydration-related AKI.
hepatic: Mild impairment: monitor; moderate-severe: dose-reduce or avoid per labeling (most agents hepatically cleared).

major: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (raise exposure - reduce fedratinib to 200 mg)
moderate: Agents raising thiamine demand or causing GI losses (monitor thiamine)
interactions.food: With food (a high-fat meal is acceptable and improves GI tolerability).
interactions.alcohol: Avoid excess alcohol with hepatotoxic therapy.
interactions.diagnostics: No characteristic laboratory test interference; monitor disease-specific markers.

serious: Encephalopathy including Wernicke (boxed; can be fatal)
emergency: Confusion, unsteady walking or eye-movement problems (possible Wernicke) - seek emergency care and hold drug
Severe vomiting preventing medicines/fluids - seek urgent care

monitoring: Thiamine level before starting, periodically and with any neurologic/GI change; replete as needed
counsel: Take with food at the same time daily; report persistent nausea, vomiting or diarrhoea
Confusion, clumsiness or vision/eye changes need emergency evaluation (brain vitamin emergency)
Attend regular blood counts - transfusions may be needed
Tell the team about antifungal or other new medicines; use contraception
pk: Target inhibition within hours-days; response assessed in weeks
Approximately 41 hours (once-daily dosing; long half-life prolongs washout)
Room temperature 20-25 C in original container; protect from moisture
pearls: Thiamine monitoring is unique among JAK inhibitors - build it into every review
Wernicke presentation (confusion/ataxia/eye signs) must trigger immediate hold + parenteral thiamine
GI dosing with food is a tolerability requirement, not optional
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered on the same day unless it is near the next dose; never double up. Take as soon as remembered on the same day; do not double.
overdose: No specific antidote. Withhold drug and give supportive care with monitoring of CBC, ECG, LFTs and agent-specific toxicities. Contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222).
